brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A medicinal cold-remedy tea from Guangdong, pressed into bricks from herb-soaked leaves and also known as box tea for its small packaging.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: It was created in the Daoguang era of the Qing by the three Yuan brothers Huichang, Hechang and Yingchang under the Yuan Jilin name, and Yuan Jilin Ganhe Tea is on Guangdong's intangible heritage list. Standard versions appear in China's national drug standards, and the Yuan Jilin formula became a prescription product in 2005.
processing: Herbs are first prepared, then their decoction is absorbed into leaf that is pressed into bricks.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: A herbal infusion; the taste depends on the plant.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
